title: EvasionBench: Detecting Evasive Answers in Financial Q&A via Multi-Model Consensus and LLM-as-Judge

bias_targets.methodology: Calculating the selection frequency of the LLM judge (Claude Opus 4.5) choosing its own independently generated labels versus a different model's labels (Gemini-3-Flash) during disagreement resolution to check if the judge unfairly favors its own outputs.

Comparing the training loss and held-out test accuracy of a student model trained purely on a single teacher's labels (Opus-only baseline) versus a model trained on multi-model consensus labels to demonstrate how distillation from a single model causes overfitting to that specific model's idiosyncrasies.
